newsitem.title: USA: Texas' top Democrat to retire from politics.
newsitem.headline: Texas' top Democrat to retire from politics.

text.p: Texas' most powerful Democrat said Thursday he would retire from politics in a move that could strengthen the Republican Party's grip on the state.
Lt. Gov. Bob Bullock, 67, told reporters he would not seek re-election when his term expires in January 1999 because he wanted to spend more time with his family.

"For those in the news media who, for whatever reason, have said for years that my career wouldn't last, I have a parting message: I've outlasted the reporters, columnists, editors and publishers who started with me," he said.
"And I've outlasted the Dallas Times-Herald, the Houston Post and the San Antonio Light. End of story," Bullock said, referring to now-defunct Texas newspapers.
Bullock started his political career as a member of the state legislature in 1957. He held several top posts in state government before being elected lieutenant governor in 1990.

In that role, Bullock presides over the state senate and was the dominant figure in determining which legislation became law. He is known as a tough behind-the-scenes player not afraid to intimidate legislators to get his way.
Bullock is a moderate who was said to chafe at the increasingly conservative cast of the state senate, which this year for the first time since Reconstruction has a Republican majority.

Texas Gov. George W. Bush, a Republican, praised Bullock in a statement. "Much of Texas history has been shaped by political leaders who seem larger than life, individuals whose strength of purpose and force of personality changed the course of our state. Bob Bullock is one of them," he said.
Other top Republican officeholders in Texas include U.S. Sens. Phil Gramm and Kay Bailey Hutchison.

Unless Bush calls a special session of the state legislature, the 1997 legislative session that ended on Monday would be Bullock's last. Under Texas law the legislature meets once every two years in sessions that last four months.
